(Clause 31) AWARD 1.
The present Detailed Accident Report was filed qua the accident dated 07.02.2018.
As per the facts of the present case, on 07.02.2018, at about 3.30 p.m, the deceased Sh Vikram Singh S/O Late Sh Mool Chand was going on his motor cycle No. DL P SAQ 9082 towards Shiv Vihar Delhi.
Meanwhile the offending vehicle ( RTV) bearing No. DL1VC0091 being driven by respondent No.1 came at a very high speed rashly and negligently and hit the motor cycle of deceased with forceful impact.
Due to this impact deceased received fatal injury.
The deceased died at the hospital.
The present claim case pertains to the death of Sh Vikram Singh .

2. After investigation, investigating agency contended that the said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving of RTV bearing no. DL1VC0091 by Ajit Singh (driver), who has been made MACT No. 227/18 NITU DEVI & Ors VS AJIT SINGH & Ors Page No. 8 of 18 as respondent no. 1.

sentences.text: Sh Mukesh Kumar (owner) has been made as respondent no. 2.
And as the offending vehicle was insured with Oriental Insurance Company Limited hence it has been made as respondent no. 3.
After investigation the present DAR has been filed by the Investigating Agency.

The DAR has been considered as claim petition.
3.
The respondents have contested the present claim.
4. The respondent no. 1 and 2 have filed their joint WS stating therein that driver/R1 was driving the offending vehicle in a very slow speed and was having a valid licence.
It stated that accident took place due to rash and negligent act of deceased as he was driving his motor cycle negligently.
5. The respondent no. 3 in a written statement had submitted that the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation as offending vehicle was being ply on the road without any valid permit.

6. After completion of the pleading, following issued were framed on 12.04.2018:

sentences.text: In order to prove their claim, petitioners have examined petitioner No.1 Smt Nitu Devi as PW1 and Sh Karan, an eye witness as PW2.The
respondent No.3 has examined Ms Pallvee Thakral Assistant Manager, as R3W1 in its support.
8. I have heard ld. counsel appearing on behalf of petitioners and respondent No.3.
None appeared on behalf of R.1 and R.2 to argue the case finally.

My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE No.1: Whether Sh Vikram Singh sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt 07.02.2018 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle (RTV Bus) No.DL1 VC0091being driven by respondent No.1 Ajit Singh owned by respondent No.2 Mukesh and insured by Respondent 3 The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd ? .. OPP 9.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
To prove this issue petitioners have examined PW2 Sh Karan Singh.
PW2 has deposed that on 07.02.2018, at about 3.30 p.m, he was going towards Shiv Vihar,Delhi .
He has deposed that one ( RTV) bearing No. DL 1VC0091 came at a very high speed rashly and negligently and hit the motor cycle of deceased, Vikram Singh with forceful impact.
As a result of this impact deceased received fatal injury.
The deceased died at the hospital.

PW2 was duly crossexamined by insurance company but the testimony of the this PW with respect to accident and rash & negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 could not be impeached.

Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing MACT No. 227/18 NITU DEVI & Ors VS AJIT SINGH & Ors Page No. 10 of 18 of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/338/304A of IPC.

entities.text: MACT No. 227/18 NITU DEVI & Ors VS AJIT SINGH & Ors

sentences.text: The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof.
Therefore, the evidence which has come on the file only can be considered.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show there was any fault on the part of deceased while driving his motor cycle.
10. The fact that Sh Vikram Singh died in that accident is also supported by his postmortem report on the dead body of victim.
Moreover,after investigation, police indicted respondent no.1 as accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/304A of IPC.
The FIR has been registered against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his such implication.

Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of RTV bearing No. DL1VC0091 by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Sh Vikram Singh .

So prima facie a fact has been brought on record that driver of the offending vehicle was driving the offending vehicle rashly and Mact No. 227/18 Nitu Devi & Ors vs Ajit Singh & Ors Page No. 1 Of 18 on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148808028/

sentences.text: Petitioner no. 1 is wife of deceased Sh Vikram Singh , petitioner no. 2 and 3 are son and daughter of victim while petitioners No. 4 is the mother of deceased/victim.
13. Now coming to the extent of compensation.
According to PW1Nitu her husband was doing private job and earning Rs.25,000/ P.M.
But petitioners have not placed on record any documentary proof to show the income of the deceased.
So in the absence of any documentary evidence with regard to the income of deceased.
This Tribunal has left with no option but to assessed the income of deceased as per Minimum Wages Act.
Even Ld Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that income of the deceased has to be assessed on the basis Minimum Wages prevalent in Delhi at the time of accident.
As per Ex PW1/3 ( Colly) the deceased has passed High School examination in the year 2007.
So this Tribunal has assessed the monthly income of deceased as 16,468/ pm for computation of compensation as per Minimum Wages prevalent in Delhi at the time of accident for a matriculates.

14. As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit have to be given @ 40% is to be added in the monthly income.

sentences.text: So while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of death of the deceased is to be considered.
Reliance is placed on Sushila Devi & Ors Vs Sandeep Kumar & Ors MAC.APP.411/2015 decided by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi on 29.03.2023.

sentences.text: So deceased/victim is presumed to be spending 1/4th of his income on his personal expenses.
And therefore the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.17,291.40 ( 16,468/ + 6,587.20 - 5,763.80/) per month.
16. To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
The age of the deceased was 33 years old ( as High School examination ) A multiplier of 16 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.

Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs.
33,19,948.80/ (17,291.40 x 12 x 16. ).
So an amount of Rs. 33,20,000/ in lumpsum is allowed to petitioners as loss of dependency.

sentences.text: Now coming to the extent of liability.
It has already been held herein above that the deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
He is primarily liable to make payment.
However, the petitioners have made the respondent no.3 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no.3 to pay the compensation.
19. The only submission of Ld Counsel for insurance company is that the Insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
It is submitted that respondent No.1 was not possessing any valid permit to drive RTC on the road at the time of accident.
In this regard R3 has examined as R3W1 Ms Pallvee Thakral, who has proved the copy of insurance policy vide Ex R2W1/1.
She has deposed that the offending vehicle was being driven by R.1 in contravention of insurance policy.
She has proved copy of legal notice U/O 12 rule 8 CPC served upon R.1 and R.2 to provide the valid permit of offending vehicle.
She has deposed that no valid permit in the charge sheet was filed by the investigating officer in the criminal case.
On perusal of the permit placed on record it revealed that it is valid from 08.08.2012 to 06.08.2017.
The accident took place on 07.02.2018.

So it is proved on record that respondent No.1 was not MACT No. 227/18 NITU DEVI &
Ors VS AJIT SINGH & Ors Page No. 14 of 18 having valid permit to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

26. Whether the claimant(s) were examined at the time Yes of passing of the award.
1. Whether Sh Vikram Singh sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt 07.02.2018 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle (RTV Bus) No.DL1 VC0091 being driven by respondent No.1 Ajit Singh owned by respondent No.2 Mukesh and insured by Respondent 3 The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd ? .. OPP 2.
Whether the petitioners in the above mentioned cases are entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom ?
My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE No.1: Whether Sh Vikram Singh sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt 07.02.2018 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle (RTV Bus) No.DL1 VC0091being driven by respondent No.1 Ajit Singh owned by respondent No.2 Mukesh and insured by Respondent 3 The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd ? .. OPP 9.
This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Sh Vikram Singh had died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash and negligent driving of a RTV bearing No. DL1VC0091 by respondent no.1.
ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom ? ...
opennyai_summary.facts:
Meanwhile the offending vehicle ( RTV) bearing No. DL1VC0091 being driven by respondent No.1 came at a very high speed rashly and negligently and hit the motor cycle of deceased with forceful impact.
The deceased died at the hospital.
And as the offending vehicle was insured with Oriental Insurance Company Limited hence it has been made as respondent no. 3.
It stated that accident took place due to rash and negligent act of deceased as he was driving his motor cycle negligently.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing MACT No. 227/18 NITU DEVI & Ors VS AJIT SINGH & Ors Page No. 10 of 18 of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/338/304A of IPC.
The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof.
Therefore, the evidence which has come on the file only can be considered.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show there was any fault on the part of deceased while driving his motor cycle.
Moreover,after investigation, police indicted respondent no.1 as accused for offences punishable under Sections 279/304A of IPC.
The FIR has been registered against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his such implication.
Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of RTV bearing No. DL1VC0091 by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Sh Vikram Singh .
OPP MACT No. 227/18 NITU DEVI & Ors VS AJIT SINGH & Ors Page No. 11 of 18 12.
This Tribunal has left with no option but to assessed the income of deceased as per Minimum Wages Act.
As per Ex PW1/3 ( Colly) the deceased has passed High School examination in the year 2007.
So this Tribunal has assessed the monthly income of deceased as 16,468/ pm for computation of compensation as per Minimum Wages prevalent in Delhi at the time of accident for a matriculates.
MACT No. 227/18 NITU DEVI & Ors VS AJIT SINGH & Ors Page No. 12 of 18
So while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of death of the deceased is to be considered.
Reliance is placed on Sushila Devi & Ors Vs Sandeep Kumar & Ors MAC.APP.411/2015 decided by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi on 29.03.2023.
So deceased/victim is presumed to be spending 1/4th of his income on his personal expenses.
And therefore the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.17,291.40 ( 16,468/ + 6,587.20 - 5,763.80/) per month.
16. To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
The age of the deceased was 33 years old ( as High School examination ) A multiplier of 16 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
However, the petitioners have made the respondent no.3 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no.3 to pay the compensation.
